artifacts.title: Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because Mr. Benyola was no longer a member of any PCA congregation and thus lacked standing. The SJC approved the dismissal unanimously 23-0.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied most specifications of a complaint filed by TE Herron and others against Central Indiana Presbytery's investigative and suspension procedures, but sustained the complaint on the point that Presbytery improperly denied Herron access to Presbytery minutes while under process. The decision includes extensive discussion of pre-trial BCO 43-1 complaints ('interlocutory appeals') and the proper scope of BCO 31-10 administrative suspensions.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC conducted a full 42-hour trial of TE Daniel Herron of Central Indiana Presbytery on charges arising from allegations of sexual harassment and bullying, referred to the SJC by CIP under BCO 41. The SJC acquitted TE Herron on all charges, removed all censures and administrative suspensions imposed by CIP, and restored him to good standing as a PCA minister.

artifacts.title: Complaint: TE Art Sartorius v. Siouxlands Presbytery 2013-03 Complaint: Mr. G. Rick Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery 2013-06 Appeal: TE Stephen Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery 2013-08 Complaint of
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Art Sartorius and six others against Presbytery of Siouxlands, finding that the Presbytery erred when it approved its Judicial Commission's verdict acquitting TE Gregory Lawrence of five charges related to Federal Vision theology and unconventional views on baptism and apostasy. The SJC identified serious procedural errors, specifically that the Judicial Commission admitted exculpatory post-indictment written statements from the defendant without subjecting them to cross-examination, contrary to BCO 35-5. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial with detailed instructions regarding evidence procedures and Presbytery oversight.
